```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5, out.width = "100%")
# A number written for the text: plain for moderate sizes, and as
# m x 10^e (HTML) otherwise
fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  x <- signif(x, digits)
  if (!is.finite(x)) return(as.character(x))
  if (abs(x) < 1e-300) return("0")
  e <- floor(log10(abs(x)))
  if (e >= -3 && e <= 4) return(format(x, digits = digits, big.mark = ","))
  sprintf("%s &times; 10<sup>%d</sup>", format(x / 10^e, digits = digits),
          as.integer(e))
}
```

```{r setup}
library(onestepcox)
library(ggplot2)
```

`GenSimData()` generates two-group trials, and `CompareOC()` applies the
estimators of `EstHR()` to them and summarizes how they behave. This article
shows both.

## Simulated trials

In each trial of `GenSimData()`, subjects enter uniformly over an accrual
period of length `a`, their survival times are exponential with hazard
`hazard_C` in the control group and `HR * hazard_C` in the treatment group,
and the analysis takes place at the `E`-th event. Subjects without an event
by then are censored.

```{r one-trial}
one <- GenSimData(nsim = 1, n_T = 100, n_C = 100, hazard_C = log(2) / 18,
                  HR = 0.7, a = 12, E = 150, seed = 2)
head(one)
```

The group is a factor with levels `"T"` and `"C"`. With vectors, `EstHR()`
is told which group is the control group:

```{r one-estimate}
EstHR(one$time, one$event, one$group, control = "C",
      method = c("MH_Halley", "Cox_NR"))
```

The Kaplan-Meier curves of this trial:

```{r km, fig.alt = "Kaplan-Meier curves of the treatment and control groups of one simulated trial."}
km <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ group,
                        data = as.data.frame(one))
km_d <- data.frame(time = km$time, surv = km$surv,
                   group = rep(sub("group=", "", names(km$strata)),
                               km$strata))
# The curves start at survival 1 at time 0
km_d <- rbind(data.frame(time = 0, surv = 1, group = unique(km_d$group)),
              km_d)
ggplot(km_d, aes(x = time, y = surv, colour = group)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(x = "Time since entry", y = "Survival probability", colour = "Group") +
  theme_bw()
```

Strata with their own baseline hazards are given by `strata_prop` and
`strata_hazard`, and `time_unit` rounds the times up to multiples of a unit,
which produces tied event times.

```{r strata-ties}
two <- GenSimData(nsim = 1, n_T = 100, n_C = 100, hazard_C = log(2) / 18,
                  HR = 0.7, a = 12, E = 150, strata_prop = c(0.5, 0.5),
                  strata_hazard = c(1, 3), time_unit = 1, seed = 2)
table(stratum = two$stratum, group = two$group)
```

```{r tied, include = FALSE}
event_times <- two$time[two$event == 1]
```

In this trial, the `r sum(two$event)` events fall on
`r length(unique(event_times))` distinct times.

## Comparing the estimators

`CompareOC()` runs `GenSimData()` for each scenario (one row of a data
frame), applies `EstHR()` to each trial, and summarizes each method. The
scenarios below have hazard ratios on both sides of 1 and, in the last one,
strata and tied times. The reference for the deviations is `"Cox_NR"`, the
Cox estimate by Newton-Raphson iteration on the risk-set summaries.

```{r scenarios}
scenarios <- data.frame(
  label     = c("HR 0.5", "HR 1", "HR 2", "HR 2, strata, ties"),
  n_T       = 100,
  n_C       = 100,
  hazard_C  = log(2) / 18,
  HR        = c(0.5, 1, 2, 2),
  a         = 12,
  E         = 150,
  time_unit = c(0, 0, 0, 1)
)
scenarios$strata_prop <- list(NULL, NULL, NULL, c(0.5, 0.5))
scenarios$strata_hazard <- list(NULL, NULL, NULL, c(1, 3))
nsim <- 200
res <- CompareOC(scenarios,
                 methods = c("Cox_NR", "Cox", "MH_Halley", "MH_Newton",
                             "Pike_Halley", "MH", "Pike", "Peto"),
                 nsim = nsim, seed = 1, reference = "Cox_NR")
res
```

### Deviation from the Cox estimate

The first figure shows, for each method and scenario, a box plot of the
absolute difference from the Cox estimate over the `r nsim` trials.

```{r deviation, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Absolute deviation of each method from the Cox_NR estimate of the log hazard ratio by scenario, on a logarithmic scale."}
plot(res, what = "deviation")
```

```{r deviation-numbers, include = FALSE}
s <- res$summary
dev_max <- function(m) max(s$dev_max[s$method == m])
mis_max <- function(m) max(s$mismatch_2dp[s$method == m])
mis_text <- function(m) {
  p <- mis_max(m)
  if (p < 1e-12) return("none of the trials")
  paste("up to a proportion", fmt_num(p), "of the trials of a scenario")
}
cl <- attr(res, "conf.level")
mc_se <- sqrt(cl * (1 - cl) / nsim)
```

The largest difference of MH-Halley over all scenarios is
`r fmt_num(dev_max("MH_Halley"))`, compared with `r fmt_num(dev_max("MH"))`
for the Mantel-Haenszel estimate, `r fmt_num(dev_max("Pike"))` for the Pike
estimate, and `r fmt_num(dev_max("Peto"))` for the Peto estimate. Written
with two decimals, the hazard ratio of MH-Halley differs from that of the Cox
estimate in `r mis_text("MH_Halley")`, compared with
`r mis_text("Peto")` for the Peto estimate.

### Bias, RMSE, and coverage relative to the true hazard ratio

The next figures show the anchors and MH-Halley; MH-Halley lies on top of
the Cox estimate (`"Cox_NR"`), and the one-step corrections and `"Cox"` would
lie there too.

```{r shown, include = FALSE}
shown <- c("Cox_NR", "MH_Halley", "MH", "Pike", "Peto")
```

```{r bias, fig.alt = "Bias of the log hazard ratio of each method relative to the true value by scenario."}
plot(res, what = "bias", methods = shown)
```

```{r rmse, fig.alt = "Root mean squared error of the log hazard ratio of each method by scenario."}
plot(res, what = "rmse", methods = shown)
```

```{r coverage, fig.alt = "Coverage of the confidence intervals of each method by scenario."}
plot(res, what = "coverage", methods = shown)
```

The table gives these summaries for MH-Halley and the Cox estimate. They are
close, because the two estimates differ by far less than their standard
errors.

```{r summary-table}
tab <- s[s$method %in% c("MH_Halley", "Cox_NR"),
         c("label", "method", "bias", "rmse", "coverage", "se_mean")]
tab$method <- gsub("_", "-", tab$method)
for (v in c("bias", "rmse", "se_mean")) tab[[v]] <- sprintf("%.4f", tab[[v]])
tab$coverage <- sprintf("%.3f", tab$coverage)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrr",
             col.names = c("Scenario", "Method", "Bias", "RMSE", "Coverage",
                           "Mean SE"))
```

With `r nsim` trials, the Monte Carlo standard error of a coverage near the
nominal level `r cl` is about `r fmt_num(mc_se)`.

### Standard errors and computing time

The ratio of the standard error of each method to that of the Cox estimate:

```{r se-ratio, fig.alt = "Median ratio of the standard error of each method to that of the Cox_NR estimate by scenario."}
plot(res, what = "se_ratio", methods = setdiff(shown, "Cox_NR"))
```

The computing time per trial depends on the machine. All methods except
`"Cox"` share the risk-set summaries; `"Cox"` calls `survival::coxph()`.

```{r time, fig.alt = "Computing time per trial of each method by scenario."}
plot(res, what = "time")
```
